haiku-low.q1: The scheduler starts it at 02:00 UTC. It extracts replica orders with updated_at later than the high-water mark minus 2 hours.
haiku-low.q2: Bulk transactions stay open up to 90 minutes; updated_at is stamped at write time, not commit. Rows can appear up to 90 minutes after updated_at.
haiku-low.q3: The edit sets updated_at to write time, so the next extract picks it up and the merge upserts the newer version.
haiku-low.q4: The app sets deleted_at instead of deleting, which is a write; the merge sets is_deleted true and keeps the row.
haiku-low.q5: Nothing changes. It waits 15 minutes and reruns extract, up to three attempts total; after the third failure it pages on-call.
haiku-low.q6: Dashboards show the previous complete night. A staleness alert is posted to #data-alerts.
haiku-low.q7: The Sunday reconciliation compares each creation day in the last 30 days by count and checksum, then reloads any mismatched day through stg_orders and merge.
haiku-low.q8: The merge keeps the latest updated_at per order_id in staging and upserts only where staged updated_at is at least the stored one.
haiku-low.q9: In etl_watermark (one row). It is set to the largest updated_at extracted, in the same transaction as the merge, on success.
haiku-low.q10: A single warehouse transaction: the merge, mark advance and run status commit as a whole or not at all.
haiku-low.q11: Staged data is discarded: staging is emptied at each attempt's start. The retry extracts rows with updated_at later than the high-water mark minus 2 hours.
haiku-low.q12: Reads the replica's orders for the mismatched creation day, applies them via stg_orders and the same merge. It does not move the high-water mark.

sonnet.q1: The scheduler starts attempt 1 at 02:00 UTC. It extracts replica rows where updated_at is later than the high-water mark minus 2 hours.
sonnet.q2: Bulk-import transactions can stay open up to 90 minutes, and updated_at is stamped at write time, not commit time. So the row can become visible up to 90 minutes after its updated_at.
sonnet.q3: The edit sets a new updated_at on the replica row. A later nightly extract (updated_at > mark minus 2h) picks it up into stg_orders. The merge then upserts it into fact_orders, because the staged updated_at is at least the stored one.
sonnet.q4: A soft delete sets deleted_at and also bumps updated_at. The nightly extract picks it up and the merge sets is_deleted = true on the fact_orders row. The row is kept, not removed.
sonnet.q5: If extract fails, staging is discarded and nothing else has changed. If merge fails, the transaction rolls back. The job then waits 15 minutes and reruns from extract, up to 3 attempts in all, each with its own etl_runs row. After the third failure it pages on-call, and the mark stays where it was.
sonnet.q6: Dashboards show the previous complete night. The 06:00 check posts a staleness alert to #data-alerts.
sonnet.q7: The Sunday reconciliation. It compares per-creation-day count and checksum (order_id + updated_at) between the replica and fact_orders for the last 30 days. It reloads any mismatched day through stg_orders and the merge.
sonnet.q8: The merge keeps only the latest updated_at row per order_id in staging. It upserts into fact_orders only where the staged updated_at is at least the stored one, so older versions never overwrite newer ones. The merge is also idempotent.
sonnet.q9: It is stored in the warehouse table etl_watermark (one row). The value written is the largest updated_at extracted. It is unchanged if nothing was extracted. It is written in the same warehouse transaction as the merge, so it moves only when the data has loaded.
sonnet.q10: The merge, the mark advance and the etl_runs ok status happen in one warehouse transaction that commits as a whole or not at all. The load goes through a staging table first, so dashboards only see a whole night.
sonnet.q11: stg_orders is emptied at the start of every attempt, so the failed attempt's staged data is discarded. The retry reruns from extract. Because nothing changed the mark, it uses the same window: updated_at greater than the mark minus 2 hours.
sonnet.q12: It re-reads the replica's orders for that creation day. They go through stg_orders and the same merge, with the same upsert rule. It does not move the high-water mark.
